title: FINALLY! Classic Grumman AA-5 Series Lands in MSFS (+ 50 New Airliner Liveries)
description:
Are you looking to expand your virtual hangar in Microsoft Flight Simulator this week, or are you trying to avoid impulse buys on the storefront? Today, we break down the latest marketplace drop featuring a beloved 1970s general aviation touring family alongside two distinct airline livery collections—ranging from a multi-panel classic four-seater to over 50 real-world schemes for your commercial fleet.

To help you decide what fits your flight routine and budget, we inspect each arrival in detail:

• Blue Sky Hangar Grumman AA-5 Series: A versatile family of 1970s four-seat light touring and training aircraft, covering the Traveler, Cheetah, and Tiger variants. Built with high-detail PBR modeling and custom flight dynamics, this package delivers authentic period cockpits spanning a factory 1970s VFR panel with Collins/Bendix radios, a robust 1980s IFR suite, a 2000s modernized setup, and a rare Garmin G1000 glass cockpit configuration with Sentry 1 autopilot support.
• Two-Pilot 737-8 World Liveries Vol. 2: A massive pack of 50 international airline schemes mapped for the Boeing 737 MAX 8, adding authentic global carrier options including Austrian, Caribbean Airlines, Philippine Airlines, Icelandair, Transavia, and more.
• Perfect Flight America 250 Liveries: A standalone unbundled release offering patriotic liveries without forcing extra IFR activity files, bringing liveries to the Boeing 787-10 Dreamliner and iniBuilds A320neo V2 across carriers like American, United, JetBlue, and Southwest.

Whether you're planning a low-and-slow VFR cross-country in a classic 1970s Grumman Tiger or refreshing your airliner fleet with authentic real-world operations, we evaluate each release to help you decide what truly deserves a spot in your simulator installation.

If you enjoy honest, clear, and critical looks at the Flight Simulator Marketplace without the fluff, make sure to hit that like button, subscribe to the channel, and drop a comment below! Which of these add-ons are you picking up?
